newsitem.title: CHINA: China, UK agree on Hong Kong air service accords.
newsitem.headline: China, UK agree on Hong Kong air service accords.

text.p: China and Britain reached an agreement on Hong Kong's air services accords with Thailand and Burma, British officials said on Thursday.
They also said that China and Britain agreed to allow Hong Kong to negotiate its own overflight accords with other countries, extending beyond the transfer of power in 1997.
The agreements were reached at meetings in Beijing of the Sino-British Joint Liaison Group, set up by the two sides to handle issues linked to the return of Hong Kong to Chinese rule on July 1, 1997.
China has insisted that it must approve air services agreements for Hong Kong that extend beyond the transfer of power.

The approval of an air services accord with Thailand removes questions over continued air service on the key Hong Kong-Bangkok route, though other air pacts remain to be endorsed ahead of the handover of the colony next year.
"We still have a substantial backlog of work on air services, and little time in which to complete it," said Hugh Davies, Britain's chief official at the Joint Liaison Group.
In a reference to the overflight accord, he told reporters: "Those are of vital importance to Hong Kong's civil aviation interest and we expect negotiations to begin in the near future."
